title: JEE Main 2026 · 21 Jan · Shift 2 (recreated)

qs.stem: Let f : R → R be a twice differentiable function such that f″(x) > 0 for all x ∈ R and f′(a − 1) = 0, where a is a real number. Let g(x) = f(tan<sup>2</sup>x − 2tan x + a), 0 < x < π/2. Consider the following two statements: (I) g is increasing in (0, π/4); (II) g is decreasing in (π/4, π/2). Then,
steps: g′(x) = f′((tan x − 1)<sup>2</sup> + a − 1) · 2(tan x − 1)sec<sup>2</sup>x.
Since f″ > 0, f′ is increasing, and f′(a − 1) = 0. The argument (tan x − 1)<sup>2</sup> + a − 1 is ≥ a − 1, so f′(…) ≥ 0.
So the sign of g′ is the sign of (tan x − 1): negative on (0, π/4), positive on (π/4, π/2).
Hence g is decreasing on (0, π/4) and increasing on (π/4, π/2); both statements are false.

qs.stem: Let a, a<sub>2</sub>/2, a<sub>3</sub>/2<sup>2</sup>, …, a<sub>10</sub>/2<sup>9</sup> be a G.P. of common ratio 1/√2. If a<sub>1</sub> + a<sub>2</sub> + … + a<sub>10</sub> = 62, then a<sub>1</sub> is equal to :
steps: The first term is a = a<sub>1</sub>, so a<sub>k</sub>/2<sup>k−1</sup> = a<sub>1</sub>(1/√2)<sup>k−1</sup>, giving a<sub>k</sub> = a<sub>1</sub>(√2)<sup>k−1</sup>.
So the a<sub>k</sub> form a G.P. with ratio √2: sum = a<sub>1</sub>((√2)<sup>10</sup> − 1)/(√2 − 1) = a<sub>1</sub>·31/(√2 − 1) = 62.
Therefore a<sub>1</sub> = 2(√2 − 1).

qs.stem: Let A = {x : |x<sup>2</sup> − 10| ≤ 6} and B = {x : |x − 2| > 1}. Then :
steps: |x<sup>2</sup> − 10| ≤ 6 gives 4 ≤ x<sup>2</sup> ≤ 16, so A = [−4, −2] ∪ [2, 4].
|x − 2| > 1 gives x < 1 or x > 3, so B = (−∞, 1) ∪ (3, ∞).
B − A removes [−4, −2] and (3, 4] from B: (−∞, −4) ∪ (−2, 1) ∪ (4, ∞), which is option (4). Option (1) wrongly includes 3, (3) wrongly excludes 3 from A − B = [2, 3].

qs.stem: If the system of equations 3x + y + 4z = 3, 2x + αy − z = −3, x + 2y + z = 4 has no solution, then the value of α is equal to :
steps: Determinant of coefficients: Δ = 3(α + 2) − 1(2 + 1) + 4(4 − α) = 19 − α.
No solution needs Δ = 0, i.e. α = 19, and a nonzero Δ<sub>x</sub>.
Δ<sub>x</sub> = 3(α + 2) − 1(−3 + 4) + 4(−6 − 4α) = −13α − 5, which is −252 ≠ 0 at α = 19. So the system is inconsistent for α = 19.

qs.stem: Let z be the complex number satisfying |z − 5| ≤ 3 and having maximum positive principal argument. Then 34|(5z − 12)/(5iz + 16)|<sup>2</sup> is equal to :
steps: z lies in the disc centred at 5 of radius 3. Maximum argument occurs at the tangent from the origin, length √(25 − 9) = 4, with tanθ = 3/4.
So z = 4(cosθ + i sinθ) = 16/5 + 12i/5, i.e. 5z = 16 + 12i.

qs.stem: Let y = y(x) be the solution of the differential equation sec x (dy/dx) − 2y = 2 + 3 sin x, x ∈ (−π/2, π/2), y(0) = −7/4. Then y(π/6) is equal to :
steps: Divide by sec x: dy/dx − (2cos x)y = (2 + 3 sin x)cos x, a linear equation with integrating factor e<sup>−2 sin x</sup>.
Put t = sin x: ∫(2 + 3t)e<sup>−2t</sup>dt = −(2 + 3t)e<sup>−2t</sup>/2 − (3/4)e<sup>−2t</sup>, so y = −(2 + 3 sin x)/2 − 3/4 + Ce<sup>2 sin x</sup>.
y(0) = −1 − 3/4 + C = −7/4 gives C = 0.
y(π/6) = −(2 + 3/2)/2 − 3/4 = −7/4 − 3/4 = −5/2.

qs.stem: Let A = {2, 3, 5, 7, 9}. Let R be the relation on A defined by xRy if and only if 2x ≤ 3y. Let l be the number of elements in R, and m be the minimum number of elements required to be added in R to make it a symmetric relation. Then l + m is equal to :
steps: Count y with y ≥ 2x/3 for each x: x = 2 gives 5, x = 3 gives 5, x = 5 (y ≥ 10/3) gives 3, x = 7 (y ≥ 14/3) gives 3, x = 9 (y ≥ 6) gives 2. So l = 18.

qs.stem: If the line αx + 4y = √7, where α ∈ R, touches the ellipse 3x<sup>2</sup> + 4y<sup>2</sup> = 1 at the point P in the first quadrant, then one of the focal distances of P is :
steps: Ellipse: x<sup>2</sup>/(1/3) + y<sup>2</sup>/(1/4) = 1, so a<sup>2</sup> = 1/3, b<sup>2</sup> = 1/4. Tangency c<sup>2</sup> = a<sup>2</sup>m<sup>2</sup> + b<sup>2</sup> with m = −α/4, c = √7/4: 7/16 = α<sup>2</sup>/48 + 1/4, so α<sup>2</sup> = 9, and α = 3 for a first-quadrant contact.
Tangent at (x<sub>1</sub>, y<sub>1</sub>): 3x<sub>1</sub>x + 4y<sub>1</sub>y = 1. Matching with 3x + 4y = √7 gives x<sub>1</sub> = y<sub>1</sub> = 1/√7.
Eccentricity e = √(1 − 3/4) = 1/2. Focal distances are a ± ex<sub>1</sub> = 1/√3 ± 1/(2√7).
The sum form 1/√3 + 1/(2√7) is option (2).

qs.stem: Let the line L pass through the point (−3, 5, 2) and make equal angles with the positive coordinate axes. If the distance of L from the point (−2, r, 1) is √(14/3), then the sum of all possible values of r is :
steps: Direction of L is (1, 1, 1). Vector from (−3, 5, 2) to (−2, r, 1) is v = (1, r − 5, −1).
Distance<sup>2</sup> = |v|<sup>2</sup> − (v·d)<sup>2</sup>/3 = 2 + (r − 5)<sup>2</sup> − (r − 5)<sup>2</sup>/3 = 14/3.
So (2/3)(r − 5)<sup>2</sup> = 8/3, (r − 5)<sup>2</sup> = 4, r = 3 or 7.
Sum = 10.

qs.stem: Let the line L1 be parallel to the vector −3i + 2j + 4k and pass through the point (2, 6, 7), and the line L2 be parallel to the vector 2i + j + 3k and pass through the point (4, 3, 5). If the line L3 is parallel to the vector −3i + 5j + 16k and intersects the lines L1 and L2 at the points C and D, respectively, then |CD|2 is equal to :
steps: C = (2 − 3λ, 6 + 2λ, 7 + 4λ), D = (4 + 2μ, 3 + μ, 5 + 3μ). D − C = (2 + 2μ + 3λ, −3 + μ − 2λ, −2 + 3μ − 4λ) must be parallel to (−3, 5, 16).
Equating ratios gives 13μ + 9λ + 1 = 0 and μ − 12λ − 38 = 0, so λ = −3, μ = 2.

qs.stem: The largest n ∈ N, for which 7<sup>n</sup> divides 101!, is :
steps: Exponent of 7 in 101! by Legendre's formula: ⌊101/7⌋ + ⌊101/49⌋ + ⌊101/343⌋.

qs.stem: For a triangle ABC, let p = BC, q = CA and r = BA (vectors). If |p| = 2√3, |q| = 2 and cosθ = 1/√3, where θ is the angle between p and q, then |p × (q − 3r)|2 + 3|r|2 is equal to :
steps: BC + CA = BA, so r = p + q. Then q − 3r = −3p − 2q, and p × (−3p − 2q) = −2(p × q).
|p × q|2 = p2q2sin2θ = 12 · 4 · (2/3) = 32, so the first term is 4 × 32 = 128.

qs.stem: Let one end of a focal chord of the parabola y<sup>2</sup> = 16x be (16, 16). If P(α, β) divides this focal chord internally in the ratio 5 : 2, then the minimum value of α + β is equal to :
steps: Parameter of (16, 16) on y<sup>2</sup> = 16x is t = 2 (point (4t<sup>2</sup>, 8t)). For a focal chord t<sub>1</sub>t<sub>2</sub> = −1, so the other end has t = −1/2: (1, −4).
The ratio may be taken from either end. From (16, 16): P = (5(1, −4) + 2(16, 16))/7 = (37/7, 12/7), sum 7. From (1, −4): P = (2(1, −4) + 5(16, 16))/7 = (82/7, 72/7), sum 22.
Minimum of α + β is 7.

qs.stem: The positive integer n, for which the solutions of the equation x(x + 2) + (x + 2)(x + 4) + … + (x + 2n − 2)(x + 2n) = 8n/3 are two consecutive even integers, is :
steps: Put x = 2u: 4[u(u+1) + (u+1)(u+2) + … + (u+n−1)(u+n)] = 8n/3, so the bracket sum is 2n/3 and u gives consecutive integers.
Sum of (u+k−1)(u+k) for k = 1..n equals nu<sup>2</sup> + n<sup>2</sup>u + n(n<sup>2</sup>−1)/3 = 2n/3, i.e. u<sup>2</sup> + nu + (n<sup>2</sup> − 3)/3 = 0.
Roots differ by 1, so the discriminant is 1: n<sup>2</sup> − 4(n<sup>2</sup> − 3)/3 = 1, giving n<sup>2</sup> = 9, n = 3.

qs.stem: A random variable X takes values 0, 1, 2, 3 with probabilities (2a + 1)/30, (8a − 1)/30, (4a + 1)/30, b respectively, where a, b ∈ R. Let μ and σ respectively be the mean and standard deviation of X such that σ<sup>2</sup> + μ<sup>2</sup> = 2. Then a/b is equal to :
steps: Probabilities sum to 1: (14a + 1)/30 + b = 1, so b = (29 − 14a)/30.
Setting this equal to 2: 264 − 102a = 60, a = 2, b = 1/30.

qs.stem: Let y<sup>2</sup> = 12x be the parabola with its vertex at O. Let P be a point on the parabola and A be a point on the x-axis such that ∠OPA = 90°. Then the locus of the centroid of such triangles OPA is :
steps: Take P = (3t<sup>2</sup>, 6t) and A = (λ, 0). OP ⊥ PA: (2/t)·(−6t/(λ − 3t<sup>2</sup>)) = −1, so λ = 12 + 3t<sup>2</sup>.
Centroid (h, k): h = (3t<sup>2</sup> + λ)/3 = 2t<sup>2</sup> + 4, k = 6t/3 = 2t.
Eliminate t: h = k<sup>2</sup>/2 + 4, so y<sup>2</sup> = 2x − 8, i.e. y<sup>2</sup> − 2x + 8 = 0.

qs.stem: For the matrices A = [[3, −4], [1, −1]] and B = [[−29, 49], [−13, 18]], if (A<sup>15</sup> + B)[x, y]<sup>T</sup> = [0, 0]<sup>T</sup>, then among the following which one is true :
steps: A − I = N = [[2, −4], [1, −2]] and N<sup>2</sup> = 0, so A<sup>n</sup> = I + nN = [[1 + 2n, −4n], [n, 1 − 2n]].
Both rows give 2x − 11y = 0; only x = 11, y = 2 satisfies it.

qs.stem: If the area of the region {(x, y) : 1 − 2x ≤ y ≤ 4 − x<sup>2</sup>, x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0} is α/β, α, β ∈ N, gcd(α, β) = 1, then the value of (α + β) is :
steps: Lower boundary is y = 1 − 2x for 0 ≤ x ≤ 1/2 and y = 0 for x ≥ 1/2; the upper boundary is y = 4 − x<sup>2</sup> up to x = 2.
Area = ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>1/2</sup>(3 + 2x − x<sup>2</sup>)dx + ∫<sub>1/2</sub><sup>2</sup>(4 − x<sup>2</sup>)dx = 41/24 + 81/24.

qs.stem: Let [•] denote the greatest integer function and f(x) = lim<sub>n→∞</sub> (1/n<sup>3</sup>) ∑<sub>k=1</sub><sup>n</sup> [k<sup>2</sup>/3<sup>x</sup>]. Then 12 ∑<sub>j=1</sub><sup>∞</sup> f(j) is equal to ______.
steps: Write [k<sup>2</sup>/3<sup>x</sup>] = k<sup>2</sup>/3<sup>x</sup> − {…}; the fractional parts contribute at most n terms below 1, so they vanish after dividing by n<sup>3</sup>.
f(x) = (1/3<sup>x</sup>) lim (1/n)∑(k/n)<sup>2</sup> = (1/3<sup>x</sup>)∫<sub>0</sub><sup>1</sup>t<sup>2</sup>dt = 1/3<sup>x+1</sup>.

qs.stem: If (1/<sup>15</sup>C<sub>0</sub> + 1/<sup>15</sup>C<sub>1</sub>)(1/<sup>15</sup>C<sub>1</sub> + 1/<sup>15</sup>C<sub>2</sub>)…(1/<sup>15</sup>C<sub>12</sub> + 1/<sup>15</sup>C<sub>13</sub>) = α<sup>13</sup>/(<sup>14</sup>C<sub>0</sub> · <sup>14</sup>C<sub>1</sub> … <sup>14</sup>C<sub>12</sub>), then 30α is equal to ______.
steps: For n = 15: 1/C(15, r−1) + 1/C(15, r) = 16/(r · C(15, r)), and r · C(15, r) = 15 · C(14, r−1).
So each factor equals (16/15)/C(14, r−1) for r = 1, …, 13.
The product of the 13 factors is (16/15)<sup>13</sup>/(<sup>14</sup>C<sub>0</sub> … <sup>14</sup>C<sub>12</sub>), so α = 16/15 and 30α = 32.

qs.stem: Let the maximum value of (sin<sup>−1</sup>x)<sup>2</sup> + (cos<sup>−1</sup>x)<sup>2</sup> for x ∈ [−√3/2, 1/√2] be (m/n)π<sup>2</sup>, where gcd(m, n) = 1. Then m + n is equal to ______.
steps: Let p = sin<sup>−1</sup>x ∈ [−π/3, π/4]; cos<sup>−1</sup>x = π/2 − p.
y = p<sup>2</sup> + (π/2 − p)<sup>2</sup> = 2p<sup>2</sup> − πp + π<sup>2</sup>/4, an upward parabola with vertex at p = π/4, so the maximum is at the far endpoint p = −π/3.

qs.stem: If ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>1</sup> 4cot<sup>−1</sup>(1 − 2x + 4x<sup>2</sup>) dx = a tan<sup>−1</sup>(2) − b log<sub>e</sub>(5), where a, b ∈ N, then (2a + b) is equal to ______.
steps: Since 1 − 2x + 4x<sup>2</sup> > 0, cot<sup>−1</sup>(u) = tan<sup>−1</sup>(1/u), and 1/(1 + 2x(2x − 1)) gives tan<sup>−1</sup>(2x) − tan<sup>−1</sup>(2x − 1).
∫<sub>0</sub><sup>1</sup>tan<sup>−1</sup>(2x − 1)dx = 0 (odd function over [−1, 1] after substitution).
∫<sub>0</sub><sup>1</sup>tan<sup>−1</sup>(2x)dx = tan<sup>−1</sup>2 − (1/4)ln 5.
Multiply by 4: 4tan<sup>−1</sup>2 − ln 5, so a = 4, b = 1 and 2a + b = 9.

qs.stem: If P is a point on the circle x<sup>2</sup> + y<sup>2</sup> = 4, Q is a point on the straight line 5x + y + 2 = 0 and x − y + 1 = 0 is the perpendicular bisector of PQ, then 13 times the sum of abscissas of all such points P is ______.
steps: P is the reflection of Q in x − y + 1 = 0. For Q = (t, −5t − 2), the reflection (x, y) → (y − 1, x + 1) gives P = (−5t − 3, t + 1).
P on the circle: (5t + 3)<sup>2</sup> + (t + 1)<sup>2</sup> = 4, i.e. 13t<sup>2</sup> + 16t + 3 = 0 with two real roots, t<sub>1</sub> + t<sub>2</sub> = −16/13.
Sum of abscissas = −5(t<sub>1</sub> + t<sub>2</sub>) − 6 = 80/13 − 6 = 2/13.

qs.stem: A river of width 200 m is flowing from west to east with a speed of 18 km/h. A boat, moving with speed of 36 km/h in still water, is made to travel one-round trip (bank to bank of the river). Minimum time taken by the boat for this journey and also the displacement along the river bank are ___ and ___ respectively.
steps: Minimum time for each crossing is when the boat heads straight across: t<sub>1</sub> = 200/10 = 20 s (36 km/h = 10 m/s).
Round trip: two crossings, so T = 2 × 20 = 40 s.
River speed = 18 km/h = 5 m/s, and the boat is swept along the bank for the whole 40 s: drift = 5 × 40 = 200 m.

qs.stem: The total length of potentiometer wire AB is 50 cm in the arrangement as shown in figure. If P is the point where the galvanometer shows zero reading then the length AP is ___ cm.
steps: At the null point the 6 Ω and 4 Ω resistors form a bridge with the wire segments AP and PB, so (6)/(4) = (AP)/(PB).
AP : PB = 3 : 2, so AP = (3/5) × 50 cm = 30 cm.

qs.stem: The kinetic energy of a simple harmonic oscillator is oscillating with angular frequency of 176 rad/s. The frequency of this simple harmonic oscillator is ___ Hz. [take π = 22/7]
steps: Kinetic energy varies as sin<sup>2</sup>ωt, so it oscillates at twice the oscillator's angular frequency: 2ω = 176 rad/s.
ω = 88 rad/s.

qs.stem: A capacitor C is first charged fully with potential difference of V<sub>0</sub> and disconnected from the battery. The charged capacitor is connected across an inductor having inductance L. In t s 25% of the initial energy in the capacitor is transferred to the inductor. The value of t is ___ s.
steps: Energy left in the capacitor is 75%: q<sup>2</sup>/2C = (3/4)(q<sub>0</sub><sup>2</sup>/2C), so q = (√3/2) q<sub>0</sub>.
For an LC circuit q = q<sub>0</sub> cosωt with ω = 1/√(LC), so cosωt = √3/2 and ωt = π/6.
t = (π/6)√(LC).

qs.stem: As shown in the diagram, when the incident ray is parallel to base of the prism, the emergent ray grazes along the second surface. If refractive index of the material of prism is √2, the angle θ of prism is. (The prism's left base angle is 45° and the right base angle is θ.)
steps: The horizontal ray meets the left face (inclined 45° to the base) at an angle of incidence of 45°. Snell's law: sin45° = √2 sin r<sub>1</sub>, so r<sub>1</sub> = 30°.
Grazing emergence means the ray hits the second face at the critical angle: sin r<sub>2</sub> = 1/√2, so r<sub>2</sub> = 45°.
Apex angle A = r<sub>1</sub> + r<sub>2</sub> = 75°. Angles of the triangle: 45° + 75° + θ = 180°, so θ = 60°.

qs.stem: A spherical body of radius r and density σ falls freely through a viscous liquid having density ρ and viscosity η and attains a terminal velocity v<sub>0</sub>. Estimated maximum error in the quantity η is : (Ignore errors associated with σ, ρ and g, gravitational acceleration)
steps: Terminal velocity: v<sub>0</sub> = 2r<sup>2</sup>(σ − ρ)g/(9η), so η = 2r<sup>2</sup>(σ − ρ)g/(9v<sub>0</sub>) ∝ r<sup>2</sup>/v<sub>0</sub>.
Maximum fractional error adds the absolute contributions: Δη/η = 2Δr/r + Δv<sub>0</sub>/v<sub>0</sub>.

qs.stem: A battery with EMF E and internal resistance r is connected across a resistance R. The power consumption in R will be maximum when :
steps: P = I<sup>2</sup>R = E<sup>2</sup>R/(R + r)<sup>2</sup>.
dP/dR = 0 gives (R + r) − 2R = 0, so R = r (maximum power transfer).

qs.stem: The pulley shown in figure is made using a thin rim and two rods of length equal to diameter of the rim. The rim and each rod have a mass of M. Two blocks of mass of M and m are attached to two ends of a light string passing over the pulley, which is hinged to rotate freely in vertical plane about its center. The magnitudes of the acceleration experienced by the blocks is ___. (assume no slipping of string on pulley)
steps: Let the rim radius be R = l/2. I<sub>rim</sub> = MR<sup>2</sup> = Ml<sup>2</sup>/4; the two rods cross at the centre: I<sub>rods</sub> = 2 × Ml<sup>2</sup>/12 = Ml<sup>2</sup>/6. Total I = 5Ml<sup>2</sup>/12 = (5/3)MR<sup>2</sup>.
Pulley: (T<sub>1</sub> − T<sub>2</sub>)R = Iα = (5/3)MR<sup>2</sup>(a/R), so T<sub>1</sub> − T<sub>2</sub> = (5/3)Ma.
Blocks: Mg − T<sub>1</sub> = Ma and T<sub>2</sub> − mg = ma, so T<sub>1</sub> − T<sub>2</sub> = (M − m)g − (M + m)a.
Equate: (M − m)g = a[(M + m) + (5/3)M] = a[(8/3)M + m], so a = (M − m)g/[(8/3)M + m].

qs.stem: Keeping the significant figures in view, the sum of the physical quantities 52.01 m, 153.2 m and 0.123 m is :
steps: In addition, the result keeps as many decimal places as the least precise term; 153.2 has one decimal place.
Rounding 205.333 to one decimal place gives 205.3 m.

qs.stem: Given below are two statements : Statement I : In a Young's double slit experiment, the angular separation of fringes will increase as the screen is moved away from the plane of the slits. Statement II : In a Young's double slit experiment, the angular separation of fringes will increase when monochromatic source is replaced by another monochromatic source of higher wavelength. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
steps: Fringe width β = λD/d, so the angular fringe separation is β/D = λ/d.
It does not depend on the screen distance D, so Statement I is false.
It grows with λ, so Statement II is true.
opts: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true

qs.stem: The r.m.s. speed of oxygen molecules at 47°C is equal to that of the hydrogen molecules kept at ___ °C. (Mass of oxygen molecule/ mass of hydrogen molecule = 32/2)
steps: v<sub>rms</sub> ∝ √(T/M), so equal speeds need T/M equal.
320 K / 32 = T<sub>H</sub>/2, giving T<sub>H</sub> = 20 K.
20 K = 20 − 273 = −253 °C.

qs.stem: The energy of an electron in an orbit of the Bohr's atom is −0.04 E0 eV where E0 is the ground state energy. If L is the angular momentum of the electron in this orbit and h is the Planck's constant, then 2πL/h is ___ :
steps: Energy of the n-th orbit is E<sub>n</sub> = −E<sub>0</sub>/n<sup>2</sup> (E<sub>0</sub> taken as the positive ground-state magnitude), so 1/n<sup>2</sup> = 0.04 and n = 5.
L = nh/2π, so 2πL/h = n = 5.

qs.stem: A large drum having radius R is spinning around its axis with angular velocity ω, as shown in figure. The minimum value of ω so that a body of mass M remains stuck to the inner wall of the drum, taking the coefficient of friction between the drum surface and mass M as μ, is :
steps: The wall's normal force supplies the centripetal force: N = Mω<sup>2</sup>R.
Friction must balance weight (limiting case): μN = Mg.
μMω<sup>2</sup>R = Mg, so ω<sub>min</sub> = √(g/(μR)).

qs.stem: Two known resistances of RΩ and 2RΩ and one unknown resistance XΩ are connected in a circuit as shown in the figure. If the equivalent resistance between points A and B in the circuit is XΩ, then the value of X is ___ Ω. (2R and X are in series on the upper path, in parallel with R between A and B.)
steps: The series pair is 2R + X, in parallel with R: R<sub>eq</sub> = R(2R + X)/(3R + X).
Set R<sub>eq</sub> = X: X(3R + X) = R(2R + X), so X<sup>2</sup> + 2RX − 2R<sup>2</sup> = 0.
X = [−2R + √(4R<sup>2</sup> + 8R<sup>2</sup>)]/2 = (√3 − 1)R (positive root).

qs.stem: Consider two identical metallic spheres of radius R each having charge Q and mass m. Their centers have an initial separation of 4R. Both the spheres are given an initial speed of u towards each other. The minimum value of u, so that they can just touch each other is : (Take k = 1/(4πε<sub>0</sub>) and assume kQ<sup>2</sup> > Gm<sup>2</sup> where G is the Gravitational constant)
steps: Net potential energy at separation d: U = (kQ<sup>2</sup> − Gm<sup>2</sup>)/d. Since kQ<sup>2</sup> > Gm<sup>2</sup> there is a net repulsive barrier.
'Just touch' means both are momentarily at rest at d = 2R. Energy conservation: 2(1/2)mu<sup>2</sup> + (kQ<sup>2</sup> − Gm<sup>2</sup>)/(4R) = (kQ<sup>2</sup> − Gm<sup>2</sup>)/(2R).
mu<sup>2</sup> = (kQ<sup>2</sup> − Gm<sup>2</sup>)/(4R), so u = √[(kQ<sup>2</sup>/(4mR))(1 − Gm<sup>2</sup>/(kQ<sup>2</sup>))].

qs.stem: A body of mass 2 kg is moving along x-direction such that its displacement as function of time is given by x(t) = αt<sup>2</sup> + βt + γ m, where α = 1 m/s<sup>2</sup>, β = 1 m/s, γ = 1 m. The work done on the body during the time interval t = 2 s to t = 3 s, is ___ J.
steps: v = dx/dt = 2t + 1, so v(2) = 5 m/s and v(3) = 7 m/s.
Work = change in kinetic energy = (1/2)(2)(7<sup>2</sup> − 5<sup>2</sup>) = 49 − 25 = 24 J.

qs.stem: An electromagnetic wave of frequency 100 MHz propagates through a medium of conductivity, σ = 10 mho/m. The ratio of maximum conduction current density to maximum displacement current density is ___ . [Take 1/(4πε<sub>0</sub>) = 9 × 10<sup>9</sup> N m<sup>2</sup>/C<sup>2</sup>]
steps: With E = E<sub>0</sub> sinωt: J<sub>c</sub>(max) = σE<sub>0</sub> and J<sub>d</sub>(max) = ε<sub>0</sub>ωE<sub>0</sub>.
Ratio = σ/(ε<sub>0</sub>ω), with ε<sub>0</sub> = 1/(4π × 9 × 10<sup>9</sup>) and ω = 2π × 10<sup>8</sup>.
Ratio = 10 × 4π × 9 × 10<sup>9</sup>/(2π × 10<sup>8</sup>) = 10 × 2 × 90 = 1800.

qs.stem: In a Young's double slit experiment set up, the two slits are kept 0.4 mm apart and screen is placed at 1 m from slits. If a thin transparent sheet of thickness 20 µm is introduced in front of one of the slits then center bright fringe shifts by 20 mm on the screen. The refractive index of transparent sheet is given by α/10, where α is ___ .
steps: Central fringe shift y = (μ − 1)tD/d, so μ − 1 = yd/(tD).
μ − 1 = (20 × 10<sup>−3</sup> × 0.4 × 10<sup>−3</sup>)/(20 × 10<sup>−6</sup> × 1) = 0.4.

qs.stem: A particle having electric charge 3 × 10<sup>−19</sup> C and mass 6 × 10<sup>−27</sup> kg is accelerated by applying an electric potential of 1.21 V. Wavelength of the matter wave associated with the particle is α × 10<sup>−12</sup> m. The value of α is ___ . (Take Planck's constant = 6.6 × 10<sup>−34</sup> J.s)
steps: λ = h/√(2mqV).
2mqV = 2 × 6 × 10<sup>−27</sup> × 3 × 10<sup>−19</sup> × 1.21 = 43.56 × 10<sup>−46</sup>, whose root is 6.6 × 10<sup>−23</sup>.
λ = 6.6 × 10<sup>−34</sup>/6.6 × 10<sup>−23</sup> = 10<sup>−11</sup> m = 10 × 10<sup>−12</sup> m, so α = 10.

qs.stem: A diatomic gas (γ = 1.4) does 100 J of work when it is expanded isobarically. Then the heat given to the gas ___ J.
steps: γ = 1.4 means C<sub>p</sub> = (7/2)R and C<sub>v</sub> = (5/2)R.
Isobaric work W = nRΔT = 100 J.
Q = nC<sub>p</sub>ΔT = (7/2)nRΔT = 3.5 × 100 = 350 J.

qs.stem: The terminal velocity of a metallic ball of radius 6 mm in a viscous fluid is 20 cm/s. The terminal velocity of another ball of same material and having radius 3 mm in the same fluid will be ___ cm/s.
steps: Terminal velocity v ∝ r<sup>2</sup> (same material and fluid).
v<sub>2</sub> = 20 × (3/6)<sup>2</sup> = 20/4 = 5 cm/s.

qs.stem: The correct increasing order of C−H (A), C−O (B), C=O (C) and C≡N (D) bonds in terms of covalent bond length is:
steps: Typical bond lengths: C−H about 107-109 pm, C≡N about 116 pm, C=O about 121 pm, C−O single about 143 pm.
Ascending order of length: C−H < C≡N < C=O < C−O, i.e. A < D < C < B.

qs.stem: Decomposition of A is a first order reaction at T(K) and is given by A(g) → B(g) + C(g). In a closed 1 L vessel, 1 bar A(g) is allowed to decompose at T(K). After 100 minutes, the total pressure was 1.5 bar. What is the rate constant (in min<sup>−1</sup>) of the reaction? (log 2 = 0.3)
steps: If x bar of A reacts, the total pressure is (1 − x) + x + x = 1 + x = 1.5, so x = 0.5 bar and P<sub>A</sub> = 0.5 bar.
k = 6.9 × 10<sup>−3</sup> min<sup>−1</sup>.

qs.stem: Given below are four compounds: (a) n-propyl chloride (b) iso-propyl chloride (c) sec-butyl chloride (d) neo-pentyl chloride. Percentage of carbon in the one which exhibits optical isomerism is:
steps: Only sec-butyl chloride, CH<sub>3</sub>CH(Cl)CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>3</sub>, has a chiral carbon (four different groups), so it is optically active.
Its formula is C<sub>4</sub>H<sub>9</sub>Cl, molar mass = 48 + 9 + 35.5 = 92.5 g/mol.

qs.stem:
Match List - I with List - II.
List - I (Pair of Compounds): A. 2-Methylpropene and but-1-ene; B. Cis-but-2-ene and trans-but-2-ene; C. 2-Butanol and diethyl ether; D. But-1-ene and but-2-ene.
List - II (Type of Isomers): I. Stereoisomers; II. Position isomers; III. Chain isomers; IV. Functional group isomers.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
steps: A: 2-methylpropene (branched) and but-1-ene (straight chain), both C<sub>4</sub>H<sub>8</sub>, differ in the carbon skeleton: chain isomers (III).
B: cis and trans but-2-ene differ only in spatial arrangement: stereoisomers (I).
C: 2-butanol (alcohol) and diethyl ether (ether), both C<sub>4</sub>H<sub>10</sub>O: functional group isomers (IV).
D: but-1-ene and but-2-ene differ in the position of the double bond: position isomers (II). So A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

qs.stem: Consider the following data: Δ<sub>f</sub>H°(methane, g) = −X kJ mol<sup>−1</sup>; enthalpy of sublimation of graphite = Y kJ mol<sup>−1</sup>; dissociation enthalpy of H<sub>2</sub> = Z kJ mol<sup>−1</sup>. The bond enthalpy of the C−H bond is given by:
steps: Form CH<sub>4</sub> from C(graphite) + 2H<sub>2</sub>: atomise C (+Y) and 2 H<sub>2</sub> (+2Z) to give C(g) + 4H(g).
Forming four C−H bonds releases 4ε (ε = C−H bond enthalpy), so overall Y + 2Z − 4ε = −X.
ε = (X + Y + 2Z)/4.

qs.stem:
The correct statements are:
A. Activation energy for enzyme catalysed hydrolysis of sucrose is lower than that of acid catalysed hydrolysis.
B. During denaturation, secondary and tertiary structures of a protein are destroyed but primary structure remains intact.
C. Nucleotides are joined together by glycosidic linkage between C1 and C4 carbons of the pentose sugar.
D. Quaternary structure of proteins represents overall folding of the polypeptide chain.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
steps: A is true: enzymes lower the activation energy far more (about 2-3 kJ/mol for sucrase versus about 108 kJ/mol for acid hydrolysis).
B is true: denaturation breaks hydrogen bonds and other weak forces, so secondary and tertiary structure are lost while peptide bonds (primary structure) stay.
C is false: nucleotides are linked by phosphodiester bonds between C-3′ and C-5′ of sugars, not glycosidic links between C<sub>1</sub> and C<sub>4</sub>.
D is false: overall folding of a single chain is tertiary structure; quaternary structure is the arrangement of several subunits. So only A and B.

qs.stem:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The correct order in terms of bond dissociation enthalpy is Cl2 > Br2 > F2 > I2.
Statement II: The correct trend in the covalent character of the metal halides is [SnCl4 > SnCl2], [PbCl4 > PbCl2] and [UF4 > UF6].
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
steps: Statement I: bond enthalpies are Cl<sub>2</sub> (242) > Br<sub>2</sub> (193) > F<sub>2</sub> (158, weak because of lone-pair repulsion) > I<sub>2</sub> (151) kJ/mol, so it is true.

Statement II: by Fajans' rules a higher oxidation state of the metal means greater polarising power and more covalent character. SnCl<sub>4</sub> and PbCl<sub>4</sub> are indeed more covalent than the dichlorides, but UF<sub>6</sub> (U in +6) is more covalent than UF<sub>4</sub>, so the third pair is reversed and II is false.
opts: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true

qs.stem: On heating a mixture of common salt and K<sub>2</sub>Cr<sub>2</sub>O<sub>7</sub> in equal amount along with concentrated H<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub> in a test tube, a gas is evolved. Formula of the gas evolved and oxidation state of the central metal atom in the gas respectively are:
steps: This is the chromyl chloride test: NaCl + K<sub>2</sub>Cr<sub>2</sub>O<sub>7</sub> + conc. H<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub> gives deep red fumes of CrO<sub>2</sub>Cl<sub>2</sub>.
In CrO<sub>2</sub>Cl<sub>2</sub>: x + 2(−2) + 2(−1) = 0, so Cr is +6.

qs.stem:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The correct order in terms of atomic/ionic radii is Al > Mg > Mg2+ > Al3+.
Statement II: The correct order in terms of the magnitude of electron gain enthalpy is Cl > Br > S > O.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
steps: Statement I: across period 3 atomic size decreases, so Mg (160 pm) is larger than Al (143 pm). The order Al > Mg is wrong, so I is false.
Statement II: electron gain enthalpy magnitudes (kJ/mol): Cl 349 > Br 325 > S 200 > O 141, so II is true.
opts: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true

qs.stem:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Crystal Field Stabilization Energy (CFSE) of [Cr(H2O)6]2+ is greater than that of [Mn(H2O)6]2+.
Statement II: Potassium ferricyanide has a greater spin-only magnetic moment than sodium ferrocyanide.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
steps: Statement I: H<sub>2</sub>O is a weak-field ligand. Cr<sup>2+</sup> is d<sup>4</sup> (t<sub>2g</sub><sup>3</sup>e<sub>g</sub><sup>1</sup>), CFSE = −0.6Δ<sub>o</sub>; Mn<sup>2+</sup> is high-spin d<sup>5</sup>, CFSE = 0. So I is true.

Statement II: K<sub>3</sub>[Fe(CN)<sub>6</sub>] has low-spin Fe<sup>3+</sup> (d<sup>5</sup>, 1 unpaired electron, μ = √3 = 1.73 BM); Na<sub>4</sub>[Fe(CN)<sub>6</sub>] has low-spin Fe<sup>2+</sup> (d<sup>6</sup>, 0 unpaired, μ = 0). So II is true.
opts: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false

qs.stem: Aqueous HCl reacts with MnO<sub>2</sub>(s) to form MnCl<sub>2</sub>(aq), Cl<sub>2</sub>(g) and H<sub>2</sub>O(l). What is the weight (in g) of Cl<sub>2</sub> liberated when 8.7 g of MnO<sub>2</sub>(s) is reacted with excess aqueous HCl solution? (Given molar mass in g mol<sup>−1</sup>: Mn = 55, Cl = 35.5, O = 16, H = 1)
steps: MnO<sub>2</sub> + 4HCl → MnCl<sub>2</sub> + Cl<sub>2</sub> + 2H<sub>2</sub>O, so 1 mol MnO<sub>2</sub> gives 1 mol Cl<sub>2</sub>.
Moles of MnO<sub>2</sub> = 8.7/87 = 0.1 mol, so Cl<sub>2</sub> = 0.1 mol.
Mass = 0.1 × 71 = 7.1 g.

qs.stem: Nitrobenzene is subjected to the sequence: (1) Br<sub>2</sub>/FeBr<sub>3</sub>/Δ; (2) Sn/HCl/Δ; (3) pH neutralisation; (4) Br<sub>2</sub>/H<sub>2</sub>O; (5) NaNO<sub>2</sub>/HBr, 0-5°C; (6) CuBr/NaBr, giving the major product (P). The number of bromine atom(s) in the final product (P) will be:
steps: Bromination of nitrobenzene (meta director) gives m-bromonitrobenzene; Sn/HCl then neutralisation gives m-bromoaniline.
Br<sub>2</sub>/H<sub>2</sub>O brominates the three positions ortho/para to NH<sub>2</sub> (2, 4, 6), giving 2,3,4,6-tetrabromoaniline (4 Br).
Diazotisation then CuBr (Sandmeyer) replaces the diazonium group by Br, giving pentabromobenzene with 5 Br atoms.

qs.stem:
Match list - I with List - II.
List - I (Reagents): A. H2, Pd-BaSO4; B. SnCl2, HCl; C. CrO2Cl2, CS2; D. CO, HCl, Anhyd. AlCl3.
List - II (Reaction name, involving aldehydes): I. Etard Reaction; II. Rosenmund Reduction; III. Gatterman-Koch Reaction; IV. Stephen Reaction.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
steps: H<sub>2</sub>/Pd-BaSO<sub>4</sub> (poisoned catalyst) reduces acid chlorides to aldehydes: Rosenmund (II).
SnCl<sub>2</sub>/HCl reduces nitriles to imine salts then aldehydes: Stephen (IV).
CrO<sub>2</sub>Cl<sub>2</sub> in CS<sub>2</sub> oxidises toluene to benzaldehyde: Etard (I).
CO + HCl with AlCl<sub>3</sub> formylates benzene: Gattermann-Koch (III). So A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III.

qs.stem: Consider the following spectral lines for atomic hydrogen: A. First line of Paschen series; B. Second line of Balmer series; C. Third line of Paschen series; D. Fourth line of Brackett series. The correct arrangement of the above lines in ascending order of energy is:
steps: Energy ∝ (1/n<sub>1</sub><sup>2</sup> − 1/n<sub>2</sub><sup>2</sup>). Lines: A is 3→4, B is 2→4, C is 3→6, D is 4→8.
Ascending order: D < A < C < B.

qs.stem: The correct order of the rate of the reaction for the following reaction with respect to nucleophiles is: CH<sub>3</sub>Br + Nu<sup>−</sup> → CH<sub>3</sub>Nu + Br<sup>−</sup>
steps: For an S<sub>N</sub>2 reaction on CH<sub>3</sub>Br the rate rises with nucleophilicity, which falls as the negative charge is better stabilised (delocalised).
Stability of the anion increases in the order OH<sup>−</sup> < PhO<sup>−</sup> < CH<sub>3</sub>COO<sup>−</sup> < ClO<sub>4</sub><sup>−</sup> (resonance over 0, 1 ring, 2 O, 4 O).
So nucleophilicity: OH<sup>−</sup> > PhO<sup>−</sup> > CH<sub>3</sub>COO<sup>−</sup> > ClO<sub>4</sub><sup>−</sup>.

qs.stem: By usual analysis, 1.00 g of compound (X) gave 1.79 g of magnesium pyrophosphate. The percentage of phosphorus in compound (X) is: (nearest integer) (Given, molar mass in g mol<sup>−1</sup>: O = 16, Mg = 24, P = 31)
steps: Mg<sub>2</sub>P<sub>2</sub>O<sub>7</sub> has molar mass 2(24) + 2(31) + 7(16) = 222 g/mol and contains 62 g P per mole.
Mass of P = (62/222) × 1.79 ≈ 0.50 g.

qs.stem:
Given below are some of the statements about Mn and Mn2O7. Identify the correct statements.
A. Mn forms the oxide Mn2O7, in which Mn is in its highest oxidation state.
B. Oxygen stabilizes the Mn in higher oxidation states by forming multiple bonds with Mn.
C. Mn2O7 is an ionic oxide.
D. The structure of Mn2O7 consists of one bridged oxygen.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
steps: A true: in Mn<sub>2</sub>O<sub>7</sub> Mn is +7, the group oxidation state (highest).
B true: oxygen forms multiple (pπ-dπ) bonds with Mn, which stabilises the high oxidation states.
C false: because of the high oxidation state (Fajans), Mn<sub>2</sub>O<sub>7</sub> is covalent, a volatile green oily liquid.
D true: it is O<sub>3</sub>Mn-O-MnO<sub>3</sub>, two MnO<sub>3</sub> units sharing a single bridging oxygen. So A, B, D.
opts: A, B and C and D

qs.stem: A substance 'X' (1.5 g) dissolved in 150 g of a solvent 'Y' (molar mass = 300 g mol<sup>−1</sup>) led to an elevation of the boiling point by 0.5 K. The relative lowering in the vapour pressure of the solvent 'Y' is ________ × 10<sup>−2</sup>. (nearest integer) [Given: K<sub>b</sub> of the solvent = 5.0 K kg mol<sup>−1</sup>] Assume the solution to be dilute and no association or dissociation of X takes place in solution.
steps: ΔT<sub>b</sub> = K<sub>b</sub>m gives m = 0.5/5.0 = 0.1 mol/kg.
Moles of X in 0.150 kg solvent = 0.1 × 0.150 = 0.015 mol; moles of solvent = 150/300 = 0.5 mol.
Relative lowering = n<sub>X</sub>/n<sub>Y</sub> = 0.015/0.5 = 0.03 = 3 × 10<sup>−2</sup>.

qs.stem: MX is a sparingly soluble salt that follows the given solubility equilibrium at 298 K: MX(s) ⇄ M<sup>+</sup>(aq) + X<sup>−</sup>(aq); K<sub>sp</sub> = 10<sup>−10</sup>. If the standard reduction potential for M<sup>+</sup>(aq) + e<sup>−</sup> → M(s) is (E°<sub>M<sup>+</sup>/M</sub>) = 0.79 V, then the value of the standard reduction potential for the metal/metal insoluble salt electrode E°<sub>X<sup>−</sup>/MX(s)/M</sub> is ________ mV. (nearest integer) [Given: 2.303RT/F = 0.059 V]
steps: For MX(s) + e<sup>−</sup> → M(s) + X<sup>−</sup>, the Nernst equation for M<sup>+</sup>/M gives E = E°<sub>M<sup>+</sup>/M</sub> + 0.059 log[M<sup>+</sup>], with [M<sup>+</sup>] = K<sub>sp</sub>/[X<sup>−</sup>].
At [X<sup>−</sup>] = 1 (standard state): E° = 0.79 + 0.059 log(10<sup>−10</sup>) = 0.79 − 0.59.

qs.stem: The osmotic pressure of a living cell is 12 atm at 300 K. The strength of sodium chloride solution that is isotonic with the living cell at this temperature is ______ g L<sup>−1</sup>. (Nearest integer) Given: R = 0.08 L atm K<sup>−1</sup> mol<sup>−1</sup>. Assume complete dissociation of NaCl. (Given: Molar mass of Na and Cl are 23 and 35.5 g mol<sup>−1</sup> respectively.)
steps: Isotonic means the same osmotic pressure: π = iCRT with i = 2 for NaCl.
12 = 2 × C × 0.08 × 300, so C = 12/48 = 0.25 mol/L.
Strength = 0.25 × 58.5 = 14.6 g/L, i.e. 15 to the nearest integer.

qs.stem: The first and second ionization constants of H<sub>2</sub>X are 2.5 × 10<sup>−8</sup> and 1.0 × 10<sup>−13</sup> respectively. The concentration of X<sup>2−</sup> in 0.1 M H<sub>2</sub>X solution is ______ × 10<sup>−15</sup> M. (Nearest Integer)
steps: First ionisation: [H<sup>+</sup>] = [HX<sup>−</sup>] = √(K<sub>a1</sub> × 0.1) = √(2.5 × 10<sup>−9</sup>) ≈ 5 × 10<sup>−5</sup> M.
Second ionisation is negligible, so [H<sup>+</sup>] ≈ [HX<sup>−</sup>] and K<sub>a2</sub> = [H<sup>+</sup>][X<sup>2−</sup>]/[HX<sup>−</sup>] ≈ [X<sup>2−</sup>].
[X<sup>2−</sup>] = 1.0 × 10<sup>−13</sup> M = 100 × 10<sup>−15</sup> M.

qs.stem: Identify the metal ions among Co<sup>2+</sup>, Ni<sup>2+</sup>, Fe<sup>2+</sup>, V<sup>3+</sup> and Ti<sup>2+</sup> having a spin-only magnetic moment value more than 3.0 BM. The sum of unpaired electrons present in the high spin octahedral complexes formed by those metal ions is ______.
steps: Unpaired electrons in high-spin octahedral fields: Co<sup>2+</sup> (d<sup>7</sup>) 3, Ni<sup>2+</sup> (d<sup>8</sup>) 2, Fe<sup>2+</sup> (d<sup>6</sup>) 4, V<sup>3+</sup> (d<sup>2</sup>) 2, Ti<sup>2+</sup> (d<sup>2</sup>) 2.
μ = √(n(n+2)): n = 2 gives 2.83 BM (< 3), n = 3 gives 3.87 BM, n = 4 gives 4.90 BM, so only Co<sup>2+</sup> and Fe<sup>2+</sup> qualify.
Sum of unpaired electrons = 3 + 4 = 7.
